newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Eight reported dead in Indonesian campaign.
newsitem.headline: Eight reported dead in Indonesian campaign.

text.p: At least eight people died in burning buildings and confrontations with police on the last day of campaigning for Indonesia's general elections next week, residents and news reports said on Saturday.

The official Antara news agency quoted police as saying four people died in burning buildings in the South Kalimantan provincial capital of Banjarmasin on Borneo island on Friday after a mob rampaged through the city of 400,000.
A local source said one body was found in the Hotel Kalimantan, the city's main four-star hostelry. A ground-floor shopping arcade and the four floors of the hotel itself were burned out.
Residents said the rioting erupted when partisans of President Suharto's ruling Golkar movement, campaigning through the streets, angered Moslems attending Friday prayers.

But most of the violence during last-minute campaigning was confined to Java island, home to 60 percent of the country's 200 million people. Incidents mainly involved supporters of Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).
From Banjarmasin, Reuters correspondent Jim Della-Giacoma reported that an area housing about 500 families behind a gutted church was still burning 24 hours after the riot there.
A multi-level complex in the main shopping district was also burned out. Police and troops sealed off the riot-hit areas and imposed an 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew.
Antara said at least four people died in violence at Bangil, eastern Java.
One resident contacted by phone said the four were killed during a clash between supporters of the PPP and security forces after the PPP attacked buildings.
The resident said police fired warning shots, but it was not clear exactly how the four had died. Police declined to comment.

There were no immediate reports of further trouble through the sprawling archipelago on Saturday, the start of a five-day cooling off period before an eligible 125 million voters go to the polls next Thursday to cast their ballots for the 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives.
The capital Jakarta and the satellite cities of Tangerang and Bekasi were also hit by street violence on Friday.

Antara reported other disturbances in Java at Solo and Semarang in the centre, Cirebon in the west as well as Bangil and Malang in the east. Ujung Pandang, capital of South Sulawesi province, also saw unrest.
The PPP, Golkar and the badly-split minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only three groups legally permitted to contest the elections, held every five years.
Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, took 68 percent of the vote at the last elections in 1992 and is expected to win next week's poll comfortably.
